old: When one canonical portable HumanoidMotion exists for a logical motion, the picker shows one `Humanoid` candidate for that logical motion. The UI must not arbitrarily collapse multiple non-equivalent HumanoidMotion assets by display name, target-list order, or first match. If import cannot identify one canonical portable candidate, the picker omits that synthetic grouping until the importing domain defines a deterministic source of truth. The Editor must not invent a canonical Humanoid asset on its own.
new:
The portable Humanoid candidate belongs to the logical imported motion itself. Import/reimport, not Animation Set resolution, is responsible for producing it. When enough source skeleton/profile context exists, import emits at most one canonical `HumanoidMotion` for logical motion `a`, and the picker shows exactly one `a / Humanoid` candidate. That portable variant is not created lazily when an Animation Set is assigned to a target and is not duplicated per playback target.

For a source that already contains its animation skeleton, that source rig and its usable HumanoidProfile provide the conversion context during import. For a motion-only source such as VMD, import can produce `a / x` and `a / y` only after model associations exist; the same import/reimport step must also produce `a / Humanoid` once one canonical associated Humanoid-capable model has been established for the motion source. Until such a model/profile exists, the logical motion simply has no Humanoid candidate. The importing domain, not the Animation Set picker, owns the stable provenance used for that conversion.
